duties.plain: 4. In these Directions, unless the context states otherwise, the terms here must bear the meaning assigned to them below: (1) Accounts with survivorship clause means joint deposit accounts styled as ‘either or survivor’, or ‘anyone or survivor’, or ‘former or survivor’ or ‘latter or survivor’ or any other such clause.
The number must be such that the account holder or the RRB branch where account is maintained, can't be identified by any third party.
5. An RRB must put in place approved policies and establish periodic review mechanisms to ensure sound business conduct and enhanced customer service.
8. Matters relating to customer service must be deliberated by the Board to ensure that the instructions are implemented meaningfully.
9. Customer service must be projected as a priority objective of banks along with profit, growth and fulfilment of social obligations.
An RRB must have a Board approved policy for the following: B.2.1 Deposit Policy.
10. An RRB must formulate a transparent and comprehensive policy setting out the rights of the depositors in general and small depositors in particular.
The policy must cover all aspects of operations of deposit accounts, charges leviable and other related issues to facilitate interaction of depositors at branch levels.
Such a policy must also be explicit regarding secrecy and confidentiality of customers.

11. An RRB must formulate a comprehensive and transparent policy taking into account its technological capabilities, systems and processes adopted for clearing arrangements and other internal arrangements for collection through correspondents.
The policy, among other things, must cover the following three aspects: (1) Immediate credit for local / outstation cheques.

12. An RRB must have a Board approved Customer Compensation Policy which must at a minimum, incorporate the following aspects: (1) Erroneous debits arising on fraudulent or other transactions, (2) Payment of interest for delays in collection, (3) Payment of interest for delay in issue of duplicate draft, and.
13. An RRB must ensure that wide publicity is given to the above policies formulated by it by placing them prominently on the website as well as displaying them on the notice board of its branches.
The RRB must also take necessary steps to keep the customers duly informed of the changes in the policies formulated by it when needed.
The customers must be clearly apprised of the assurances of the RRB on the services provided, at the time of establishment of the initial relationship, be it as a depositor, borrower or otherwise.

14. An RRB must constitute a Customer Service Committee of the Board and include experts and representatives of customers as invitees to enable the RRB to formulate policies and assess the compliance of it internally.

15. Customer Service Committee of the Board, illustratively, must address the following: (1) Formulation of a comprehensive Deposit Policy, (2) Issues such as the treatment of death of a depositor and operations of her / his account, (3) Product approval process with a view to suitability and appropriateness, (4) Annual survey of depositor satisfaction, and.
The Committee must also examine any other issues having a bearing on the quality of customer service rendered.
16. A detailed memorandum reviewing customer service / customer care aspects of the RRB must be placed once in every six months to the Board of Directors.
Prompt corrective action must be initiated wherever service quality / skill gaps are noticed.

17. An RRB must have a Standing Committee on Customer Service, cutting across various departments, which must serve as the micro level executive committee driving the implementation process and providing relevant feedback.
The Customer Service Committee of the Board must oversee and review / modify the initiatives.
These two Committees must be mutually reinforcing with one feeding into the other.

18. The constitution and functions of the Standing Committee must be on the lines indicated below: (1) The Standing Committee must be chaired by the Chairman and include non-officials as its members to enable an independent feedback on the quality of customer service rendered by the RRB.

(2) The Standing Committee must be entrusted not only with the task of ensuring timely and effective compliance of the Reserve Bank instructions on customer service, but also that of receiving the necessary feedback to determine that the action taken by various departments of the RRB is in tune with the spirit and intent of such instructions.
(3) The Standing Committee must, on an ongoing basis, review the practice and procedures prevalent in the RRB and take necessary corrective action.

(4) The Standing Committee must submit a brief report periodically to the Customer Service Committee of the Board on its performance during its tenure indicating, among other things, the areas reviewed, procedures/ practices identified and simplified / introduced.
(5) The Standing Committee must act as the bridge between the various departments of the RRB and the Board / Customer Service Committees of the Board.
19. An RRB must establish Customer Service Committees at branch level, which must also include their customers.
Senior citizens, an important constituent in banks, must also be included in it.

20. The Branch Level Customer Service Committee must meet at least once a month to study complaints / suggestions, cases of delay, difficulties faced / reported by customers / members of the Committee and evolve ways and means of improving customer service.

21. The Branch Level Committees must submit quarterly reports giving inputs/ suggestions to the Standing Committee on Customer Service thus enabling the Standing Committee to examine them and provide relevant feedback to the Customer Service Committee of the Board for necessary policy/ procedural action.
22. An RRB must orient its systems and procedures towards providing better customer service and must periodically assess these systems and their impact on customer service.
An RRB must have a Board approved policy for general management of the branches which must include the following aspects: -.
Business posters at semi-urban and rural branches of the RRB must also be in the concerned regional languages.
(15) Clearly establishing a new product and services approval process which must require approval by the Board, especially on issues which compromise the rights of the common person.
23. An RRB must normally function for public transactions at least for four hours on weekdays and two hours on Saturdays in the larger interest of public and trading community.
25. An RRB must keep rural branches open on weekly market day.

26. The branch managers and other supervising officials must, however, ensure that the members of the staff are available at their respective counters right from the start of banking hours and throughout the prescribed business hours so that there may not be any grounds for customers to make complaints.
An RRB must implement the recommendation taking into account the rules in the local Shops and Establishments Act.
28. An RRB must ensure that no counter remains unattended during the business hours and uninterrupted service is rendered to the customers.
Further, an RRB must allocate the work in such a way that no teller counter is closed during the banking hours at its branches.
All the customers entering the banking hall before the close of business hours must be attended to.
29. An RRB must extend business hours for banking transactions other than cash, up to one hour before the close of working hours.
30. The following non-cash transactions must be undertaken by the RRB during the extended hours, i.e.
31. Further, the non-cash transactions to be done during the extended business hours must be notified adequately for information of the customers.

33. An RRB must give to its constituent due notice about the functions to be undertaken during the extended banking hours through local newspapers, as also by displaying a notice on the notice board at the branch(es) concerned.
Further, as and when the hours of business of any of the branches are extended, the concerned clearing house must be informed.
The other staff at the branch must devote the day to keep the house keeping work up-to-date.

35. The RRB must have flexibility in fixing the non-public business working days keeping local conditions in view, especially the 'Hat' days which occupy an important place in the rural economy, subject to sufficient notice to the public / its customers of its intention.
However, the following instructions must be followed in this regard: (1) The non-public business working day must fall between two working days.
(2) All branches at places with population of 10,000 or less must be treated as rural branches.

36. The RRB must devise appropriate systems to ensure that the branch managers play an effective developmental role by undertaking as much field work as possible by prescribing a suitable diary wherein date-wise details of the villages visited, persons contacted.
Such diaries must be obtained and reviewed by the concerned controlling authorities on a regular basis and during their visits to the branches.
37. Further, the branch managers must do advance planning say, for a quarter, in regard to their visits to different villages and also keep the concerned controlling offices informed in the matter.
In particular, branch managers must ensure that harvesting seasons are effectively used for recovery of dues.
They must also devote as much time as possible on the other working days of the week for doing as much field work as possible besides attending to the office routine.

The visits to the villages must be systematically organised so that all the villages in the command area are covered at least once a quarter, by meeting as many customers as possible during each such visit taking into account the time of availability of the rural folk for such contacts.

The RRB must ensure that a perceptible improvement is recorded in the working of each rural branch as a result of introduction of one non-public business working day for recovery and healthy growth of deposits.
39. Instructions of a customer for transfer of her / his account to another branch must be carried out immediately on receipt of, and as per, her / his instructions.

It must be ensured that along with the balance of the account, the relative account opening form, specimen signatures, standing instructions, etc. or the master sheets wherever obtained, are also simultaneously transferred, under an advice to the customer.
40. The account transfer form with the enclosures must be handed over to the customer in a sealed cover if she / he so desires for delivery at the transferee branch.
However, the transferee branch must also be separately supplied with a copy of the account transfer letter.
42. An RRB must ensure that depositors dissatisfied with customer service have the facility to switch banks and thwarting depositors from such switches must invite serious adverse action.
43. An RRB must have “Enquiry” or “May I Help You” counters either exclusively or combined with other duties, located near the entry point of the banking hall.
44. An RRB must display the time norms for specialised business transactions predominantly in the banking hall.
An RRB must have a comprehensive notice board to display the information at its branches as per the format given in Annex I.

46. While displaying the information on the notice board, an RRB must adhere to the following principles: (1) The notice board must be updated on a periodical basis which must indicate the date up to which it has been updated (incorporated in the display board).
(2) Though the RRB must have discretion on pattern, colour and design of the board, the display must be kept simple and readable.
(3) The notice board must be bilingual in Hindi speaking states and trilingual in other states.
(4) The notice board must specifically indicate where recent changes have been made.
(5) The notice board must also indicate a list of items on which detailed information is available in booklet form.
47. In addition to the above board, an RRB must also display details such as ‘Name of the RRB / branch, Working Days, Working Hours and Weekly Off-days' outside the branch premises.
48. The detailed information as indicated in paragraph (E) of Annex I must be made available in various booklets / brochures as decided by an RRB.

In this connection, an RRB must also adhere to the following broad guidelines: (1) The file / folder must be kept in the customer lobby of the branch or at the ‘May I Help You‘ counter or at a place that's frequented by most customers.
Bilingual in Hindi speaking states and trilingual in other states) must be taken into account.
(3) While printing the booklets, it must be ensured that the font size is a minimum of Arial 10 so that the customers are able to easily read them.
(4) Copies of booklets must be made available to the customers on request.
49. An RRB must make available the detailed information indicated in paragraph (E) of Annex I its website.
It must be ensured that the customers are able to easily access the relevant information from the Home Page of the RRB’s website.
The RRB must adhere to the broad guidelines relating to dating of material, legibility, etc. while placing the same on its websites.
50. An RRB must display latest updated information relating to interest rates and service charges as per the format given in Annex II on its website.
The same must be easily accessible from the Home Page of its website.

52. to ensure that banking facilities percolate to the vast sections of the population, an RRB must make available all printed material used by retail customers including account opening forms, pay-in-slips, passbooks, etc. in trilingual form, i.e.
54. Wherever feasible, such messages must be displayed or distributed in the RRB branches (in the official language of the state) to enable easy notice by the customers.
An RRB must consider places like Automated Teller Machines or Business Correspondent Points where such messages could get wider visibility.
55. It needs to be emphasised that to be effective, such measures have to be pursued continuously for a long period of time and therefore the field staff must be sensitised in this regard.

The branch officials must also be encouraged to share any meaningful information (market intelligence) of any such dubious scheme in their area with their Regional Offices, which may, in turn, share such information with the respective Regional Offices of Reserve Bank.
We must ensure that all our staff members are aware of the commitments contained in these documents and faithfully implement them.
The codes to be adopted by RRBs must cover the products and services provided by the RRB in simple terminology and devoid of jargon.
59. An RRB adopting 'Codes of Fair Practices' must ensure that the availability of the codes is well publicised.
60. Besides wide initial launching publicity of the codes, the RRB must ensure that the code is displayed on Notice Board prominently in its branches and other facilities.
61. More importantly, the RRB must properly orient its staff especially its front office staff, on the relevance of codes and ensure the implementation of the codes in letter and spirit.
This number must be invariably quoted in all pay-in slips / cheques / withdrawals and correspondence with the RRB.
The passbook must be presented for withdrawal other than by cheques.
However, if due to any contingency, the passbook is required to be retained overnight, the branch will issue a receipt in the form of a paper token.
The RRB must not be held responsible for any loss or incorrect payment attributable to the neglect of this rule.
80. When a depositor wishes to withdraw money, other than by cheque book, she / he must present her / his passbook personally along with a withdrawal form prescribed by the RRB duly completed.

101. Applicants for all categories of loans irrespective of any threshold limits must be conveyed in writing within the stipulated time, the main reason / reasons which, in the opinion of the RRB have led to rejection of loan applications in the prescribed format.
(Each RRB has to prepare its own list of standard reasons for rejection and make available / circulate / display the same for the information of the customers in the notice Boards of its branches).
A copy of the loan agreement along with a copy each of all enclosures quoted in the loan agreement must also be furnished against a request in writing received from the borrower for the same.

Notice will be given in respect of any change in the terms and conditions including interest rates, service charges, etc. For this purpose, a notice on the Notice Board of the RRB's branches and offices counts as sufficient notice aside of the notices sent individually.
Changes in interest rates and charges must be effected only prospectively.
105. Post-disbursement supervision must be constructive with a view to taking care of any "lender related" genuine difficulty that the borrower may face.

106. Decision to recall / accelerate payment or performance under the agreement or seeking additional securities, RRB must be preceded by notice to borrowers, as specified in the loan agreement or a reasonable period, if no such condition exists in the loan agreement.
Where right of set off is to be exercised, borrowers must be given notice about the same with full particulars about the remaining claims.
Objection of the RRB, if any, must be conveyed within 21 days from the date of receipt of request.

112. To be entitled to the above provisions of the Fair Practices Code, the borrower agrees that: (1) She / he must abide by the assessment of credit application carried out by the RRB and must not expect the use of margin and security stipulations as a substitute for due diligence on credit worthiness of the borrower.
Appropriate interest must be charged taking into account the changes that may be effected by the RRB when needed.

114. An RRB must adhere to the instructions and procedures for opening and operating deposit accounts to safeguard against unscrupulous persons opening accounts mainly to use them as conduit for fraudulently encashing payment instruments.

However, in view of receipt of continuous complaints of fraudulent encashment by unscrupulous persons opening deposit accounts in the name/s similar to already established entities, resulting in erroneous and unauthorised debit of drawers’ accounts, an RRB must remain vigilant to prevent such lapses and issue necessary instructions to its branches / staff.

Therefore, an RRB is advised that: (1) in case of any fraud, if an RRB is convinced that an irregularity / fraud has been committed by its staff towards any constituent, the RRB must at once acknowledge its liability and pay the just claim, (2) in cases where the RRB is at fault, it must compensate customers without demur, and.

(3) in cases where neither the RRB nor the customer is at fault but the fault lies elsewhere in the system, then also the RRB must compensate the customers (up to a limit) as part of its Board approved customer relations policy.
117. The systems and procedures in RRBs must be designed to make customers feel safe about carrying out electronic banking transactions.
To achieve this, an RRB must put in place: (1) appropriate systems and procedures to ensure safety and security of electronic banking transactions carried out by customers.
118. An RRB must ask its customers to mandatorily register for SMS alerts and wherever available register for e-mail alerts, for electronic banking transactions.
The SMS alerts must mandatorily be sent to the customers, while email alerts may be sent, wherever registered.

The customers must be advised to notify their bank of any unauthorised electronic banking transaction at the earliest after the occurrence of such transaction and inform that the longer the time taken to notify the RRB, the higher will be the risk of loss to the RRB / customer.

To facilitate this, the RRB must provide its customers with 24x7 access through multiple channels (at a minimum, via website, phone banking, SMS, e-mail, IVR, a dedicated toll-free helpline, reporting to home branch, etc.) for reporting unauthorised transactions that have taken place and / or loss or theft of payment instrument such as card, etc. An RRB must also enable customers to instantly respond by "Reply" to the SMS and e-mail alerts.
As an alternative, the RRB must provide an alternate number in the transaction alert SMS itself, to which the customer can immediately send a reply.
Further, a direct link for lodging the complaints, with specific option to report unauthorised electronic transactions must be provided by the RRB on home page of its website.
The loss / fraud reporting system must also ensure that immediate response (including auto response) is sent to the customers acknowledging the complaint along with the registered complaint number.
The communication systems used by an RRB to send alerts and receive their responses to it must record the time and date of delivery of the message and receipt of customer’s response, if any, to it.
This must be important in determining the extent of a customer’s liability.
The RRB must not offer facility of electronic transactions, other than ATM cash withdrawals, to customers who don't provide mobile numbers to the bank.
On receipt of report of an unauthorised transaction from the customer, the RRB must take immediate steps to prevent further unauthorised transactions in the account.

119. A customer’s entitlement to zero liability must arise where the unauthorised transaction occurs in the following events: (1) Contributory fraud/ negligence / deficiency on the part of the RRB (irrespective of whether the transaction is reported by the customer or not).

120. A customer must be liable for the loss occurring due to unauthorised transactions in the following cases: (1) In cases where the loss is due to negligence by a customer, such as where she / he has shared the payment credentials, the customer will bear the entire loss until she / he reports the unauthorised transaction to the RRB.
Any loss occurring after the reporting of the unauthorised transaction must be borne by the RRB.

(2) In cases where the responsibility for the unauthorised electronic banking transaction lies neither with the RRB nor with the customer, but lies elsewhere in the system and the customer notifies the RRB of such a transaction within four to seven working days of receiving a communication of the transaction, the per transaction liability of the customer must be limited to the transaction value or the amount mentioned in Table 1, whichever is lower.
121. Further, if the delay in reporting is beyond seven working days, the customer liability must be determined as per the RRB’s Board approved policy.
The RRB must provide the details of its policy regarding customers’ liability formulated in pursuance of these directions at the time of opening the accounts.
The RRB must also display its approved policy in public domain for wider dissemination.
The existing customers must also be individually informed about the RRB’s policy.
123. The number of working days mentioned in Table 2 must be counted as per the working schedule of the home branch of the customer excluding the date of receiving the communication.

124. On being notified by the customer, an RRB must credit (shadow reversal) the amount involved in the unauthorised electronic transaction to the customer’s account within 10 working days from the date of such notification by the customer (without waiting for settlement of insurance claim, if any).
The credit must be value dated to be as of the date of the unauthorised transaction.
125. Further, an RRB must ensure that: (1) a complaint is resolved and liability of the customer, if any, established.

126. An RRB must formulate / revise its customer relations policy with approval of its Board, which must clearly define the rights and obligations of customers in case of unauthorised transactions in specified scenarios, i.e.

Debits to customer accounts owing to customer negligence / bank negligence / banking system frauds / third party breaches, etc. The policy must also include mechanism of creating customer awareness on the risks and responsibilities involved in electronic banking transactions and customer liability in case of unauthorised electronic banking transactions, procedure for reporting unauthorised electronic banking transactions and acknowledgement of complaints.
The instructions contained in this section must be incorporated in the policy, and the policy must be displayed prominently at branches.
127. The burden of proving customer liability in case of unauthorised electronic banking transactions must lie on the RRB.
128. An RRB must put in place a suitable mechanism and structure for the reporting of the customer liability cases to the Board or one of its Committees.
The reporting must, among other things, include volume / number of cases and the aggregate value involved and distribution across various categories of cases, viz.

Card present transactions, card not present transactions, internet banking, mobile banking, ATM transactions, etc. The Standing Committee on Customer Service in each RRB must periodically review the unauthorised electronic banking transactions reported by customers or otherwise, as also the action taken thereon, the functioning of the grievance redressal mechanism and take appropriate measures to improve the systems and procedures.
All such transactions must be reviewed by the RRB’s internal auditors.
129. An RRB must adopt / follow the principles outlined below for ensuring reasonableness in fixing and communicating service charges.
130. Identification of basic banking services: An RRB must identify basic banking services based on the following broad parameters: (1) Nature of transactions.
(a) Banking services that are ordinarily availed by individuals in the middle and lower segments, must be the first parameter.
(a) Low value transactions with customers / public up to the ceiling as given below must be the second parameter: - Remittances up to ₹10,000 in each instance.

131. Offering basic banking services outside the scope of bundled products: An RRB must make available the basic banking services at reasonable prices / charges and towards this, basic services must be delivered outside the scope of bundled products.

132. Principles for ensuring reasonableness in fixing and communicating service charges: (1) For basic services to individuals, an RRB must levy charges at the rates that are lower than the rates applied when the same services are given to non-individuals.

(2) For basic services rendered to special category of individuals (such as individuals in rural areas, pensioners and senior citizens), an RRB must levy charges on more liberal terms than the terms on which the charges are levied to other individuals.
(3) For the basic services rendered to individuals, an RRB must levy charges only if the charges are just and supported by reason.
(4) For the basic services to individuals, an RRB must levy services charges only to cover any incremental cost and subject to a cap.
(5) An RRB must provide to individual customers upfront and in a timely manner, complete information on the charges applicable to all basic services.
(6) An RRB must provide advance information to individual customers about the proposed changes in service charges.
(7) An RRB must collect for services given to individuals only such charges which have been notified to the customer.
(8) An RRB must inform its customers in an appropriate manner about recovery of service charges from the account or the transaction.

(9) An RRB, must without fail, inform its customers in all cases when a transaction initiated by the RRB itself results in or is likely to lead to a shortfall in the minimum balance required to be maintained.

The following instructions must be followed in this regard: (1) Disclosure of service charges: (i) An RRB must communicate service charges to new customers at the time of beginning of the relationship.

(ii) Service charges must be displayed in the notice board at the branch so as to disseminate information to customers / public, in addition to display on the website, as per extant instructions of the Reserve Bank.
(iii) The RRB must also put in place appropriate methods for communicating service charges to customers of different profiles.

(2) Notifying the changes effected in service charges: (i) An RRB must take steps to ensure that any change in the service charges is effected only with prior notification to customers of at least 30 days.
(ii) The RRB must provide an option to customers to accept the change.
(iv) The RRB must prominently display in the notice board as well as the website all the changes in service charges effected in the preceding 30 days.

134. Financial education: An RRB must disclose full-fledged information on its products and their implications to the customers so that the customers can make an informed judgment about their choice of products.
135. An RRB must follow a uniform, fair and transparent pricing policy and not discriminate between its customers at home branch and non-home branches.
A service provided free at the home branch must be available free at non-home branches also.

There must be no discrimination as regards intersol charges (being the charges levied by an RRB to cover the cost of extending services to customers by using the CBS / Internet / Intranet platform) between similar transactions done by customers at home branch and those done at non-home branches.
Further, an RRB must not include cash handling charges under intersol charges.
136. An RRB must leverage the technology available with it.
Every RRB must offer a BSBD account which must be considered a normal banking service available to all.
An RRB must offer the following basic minimum facilities in a BSBD account, free of charge, without any requirement of minimum balance to be maintained in such an account.
Further, no charges must be levied towards annual fee, either at the time of issuance or renewal.
Further, issuance of a continuation passbook, on exhaustion of the pages in the previous passbook, must not attract any charge.
Point of Sale transfers, NEFT, RTGS, UPI, IMPS, etc. must not be counted as withdrawals for this purpose.

The charges on digital payment transactions must be as per guidelines issued by Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Reserve Bank / National Payments Corporation of India / Government of India,.

137A. The facilities of ATM / ATM-cum-Debit card or internet / mobile banking or cheque book must be offered to a customer provided she / he requests for the same, whether at the time of opening the account or subsequently.
An RRB must not insist that a customer necessarily avails these facilities while opening and / or operating the BSBD account.
137B. In the case of existing BSBD accounts, an RRB must extend the newly introduced free facilities at clause (5) to (7) of paragraph 137 above upon receipt of a request from the customer.
The RRB must facilitate existing BSBD account holders to submit such requests through physical as well as digital channels.
However, while doing so, the RRB must not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account.
The availment of such additional facilities must be at the option of the customer.

139. Opening and operation of BSBD accounts must be subject to the instructions on Know Your Customer / Anti Money Laundering issued by the Reserve Bank through ‘ Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 ’, as amended when needed.
Further, BSBD accounts opened by or operated on behalf of minors must be subject to the instructions contained in paragraphs 229 to 234 below of these Directions.
140. An RRB, while opening a BSBD account, must not impose any requirement of an initial minimum deposit.
The RRB must convert the existing savings bank account to BSBD account within seven days of receipt of request in writing from the customer for such conversion.
Such an option must also be provided to customers through digital channels.
142. The holder of a BSBD account must not be eligible to open another BSBD account in the same RRB or any other bank.

Accordingly, before opening a new BSBD account or converting an existing savings bank account to a BSBD account, the RRB must obtain a declaration from the customer that she / he doesn't have a BSBD account in any other bank.
143. An RRB must publicise the availability of a BSBD account and its features to customers.
The RRB must also convey the differences between a BSBD account and various savings bank account variants offered by it when a customer approaches it to open a deposit account.
144. An RRB must take necessary steps to provide all its ATMs with ramps so that Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) / wheelchair users can easily access them.
Care must also be taken to make arrangements in such a way that the height of the ATMs doesn't create an impediment in their use by wheelchair users.
145. An RRB must also take appropriate steps, including providing ramps at the entrance of the branches, wherever feasible.
An RRB must report the progress made in this regard periodically to its Customer Service Committee of the Board and ensure compliance.
146. An RRB must adhere to instructions given below and extend all banking facilities to persons with blindness, low-vision and other disabilities.

(1) An RRB must ensure that all banking facilities such as cheque book facility including third party cheques, ATM facility, internet banking facility, locker facility, retail loans, credit cards etc. are invariably offered to visually impaired persons without any discrimination.
They must be assisted in withdrawal of cash.
(2) An RRB must also advise its branches to render all possible assistance to the visually impaired for availing various banking facilities.
(3) An RRB must ensure that all its ATMs are Talking ATMs equipped with Braille keypads.
(4) Magnifying glasses must also be provided in all bank branches for the use of persons with low vision, wherever they require for carrying out banking transactions with ease.
147. An RRB must extend the following facilities to account holders who are old / sick / incapacitated and who are willing to open and operate joint accounts.

149. With a view to enabling the old / sick account holders operate their bank accounts, an RRB must follow the procedure as under: (1) Wherever thumb or toe impression of the sick / old / incapacitated account holder is obtained, it must be identified by two independent witnesses known to the RRB, one of whom must be a responsible official of the RRB.

(2) Where the customer can't even put her / his thumb impression and is also unable to be physically present in the RRB, a mark can be obtained on the cheque / withdrawal form which must be identified by two independent witnesses, one of whom must be a responsible official of the RRB.
(3) The customer may also be asked to indicate to the RRB as to who would withdraw the amount from the RRB on the basis of cheque / withdrawal form as obtained above.
The person who would be actually drawing the money from the RRB must be asked to furnish her / his signature to the RRB.

150. Opinion obtained by IBA from its consultant on the question of opening of a bank account of a person who has lost both her / his hands and could not sign the cheque / withdrawal form is given below: “under the General Clauses Act, the term “Sign” with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, must with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, include “mark” with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions.
The Supreme Court has held in AIR 1950 – Supreme Court, 265 that there must be physical contact between the person who is to sign.
It can be by means of a mark which anybody can put on behalf of the person who has to sign, the mark being put by an instrument which has had a physical contact with the person who has to sign”.
The RRB must undertake appropriate measures to ensure compliance with the above Supreme Court Order,.

152. The following instructions must be applicable for the purpose of opening / operating bank accounts of the above persons: (1) The National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999 provides a law relating to certain specified disabilities.
This Act empowers a Local Level Committee to appoint a guardian, to a PwD, who must have the care of the person and property of the disabled person.

(2) An RRB must take note of the legal position stated above and must rely on and be guided by the orders / certificates issued by the competent authority, under the respective Acts, appointing guardians / managers for the purposes of opening / operating bank accounts.
In case of doubt, care must be taken to obtain proper legal advice.
153. An RRB must ensure that its branches give proper guidance to its customers so that the guardians / managers of the disabled persons don't face any difficulties in this regard.

154. An RRB must ensure that its branches display in a conspicuous place the following information in the local language and English / Hindi (or both): (1) essential details about the facilities under the enactment.

155. An RRB must put in place appropriate mechanism with the following specific provisions for meeting the needs of senior citizen and differently abled customers so that they are able to avail the RRB’s services without difficulty.
156. An RRB must provide a clearly identifiable dedicated counter or a counter which provides priority to senior citizens and people who are differently abled including visually impaired persons.

157. An RRB must ensure that when a Life certificate is submitted in any branch, including a non-home branch, of the pension paying bank, the same is updated / uploaded promptly in CBS by the receiving branch itself, to avoid any delay in credit of pension.
158. An RRB must issue cheque books to customers, whenever a request is received, through a requisition slip which is part of the cheque book issued earlier.
159. An RRB must provide minimum 25 cheque leaves every year, if requested, in a savings bank account, free of charge.
160. An RRB must not insist on physical presence of any customer including senior citizens and differently abled persons for getting cheque books.
161. An RRB must issue cheque books, on requisition, by any other mode as per the bank’s laid down policy.
162. An RRB must convert a fully KYC compliant account automatically into a ‘Senior Citizen Account’ based on the date of birth available in its records.

163. The facilities provided to sick / old / incapacitated persons through paragraphs 147 to 149 of these directions by an RRB (regarding operations of accounts through identification of thumb / toe impression / mark by two independent witnesses and authorising a person who would withdraw the amount on behalf of such customers) must also be extended to the visually impaired customers.

164. An RRB must provide Form 15G / H to senior citizens and differently abled persons once in a year (preferably in April) to enable them to submit the same, where applicable, within the stipulated time.

165. An RRB must make concerted efforts to offer certain basic banking services, such as pick up of cash and instruments against receipt, delivery of cash against withdrawal from account, delivery of demand drafts, submission of Know Your Customer (KYC) documents and Life certificate at the premises / residence of senior citizens of more than 70 years of age and differently abled persons or infirm persons (having medically certified chronic illness or disability) including those who are visually impaired.

166. An RRB must incorporate the following aspects in its Board approved policy for such services and report the progress made in this regard to the Customer Service Committee of the Board every quarter: (1) An RRB must offer doorstep banking services on pan India basis.
The RRB must develop a Board approved framework for determining the nature of branches / centres where these services will be provided mandatorily.
The list of branches offering such doorstep banking services must be displayed / updated on the bank’s website regularly.
(2) An RRB must give adequate publicity to the availability of these services in its public awareness campaigns.
The charges, in this regard, must also be prominently indicated in brochures and published on its website.
167. An RRB must ensure that demand drafts of ₹20,000 and above are issued invariably with account payee crossing.
169. Measures seeking to bring down the incidence of frauds perpetrated through RRB drafts must be built into the draft form itself.
170. All superscriptions about validity of the demand draft must be provided at the top of the draft form.
A draft must be uniformly valid for a period of three months.
171. An RRB must ensure that drafts of small amounts are issued by its branches against cash to all customers irrespective of the fact whether they are having accounts with the RRB or not.
Staff at the RRB branch counter must not refuse to accept small denomination notes from customers (or non-customers) for issuance of drafts.
172. An RRB must ensure that drafts drawn on its branches are paid immediately.
Payment of draft must not be refused for the only reason that related advice has not been received.

Further, for the delay beyond this stipulated period, an RRB must pay interest at the rate applicable for term deposit of corresponding maturity to compensate the customer for such delay.

175. The above instructions must be applicable only in cases where the request for duplicate demand draft is made by the purchaser or the beneficiary and would not be applicable in the case of draft endorsed to third parties.

176. The cheque collection policy must be integrated with the deposit policy formulated by the RRB in line with the model deposit policy of Indian Banks’ Association or Association of which it's a member.
177. The policy must clearly lay down the liability of an RRB by way of interest payments due to delays for non-compliance with the standards set by the RRB itself.
178. Compensation by way of interest payment, where necessary, must be made without any claim from the customer.

181. All cheque forms must be printed in Hindi and English.
Accordingly, cheques bearing date in Hindi as per the National Calendar (Saka Samvat) must, therefore, be accepted by an RRB for payment, if otherwise in order.
183. Both the cheque drop box facility and the facility for acknowledgement of cheques at regular collection counters must be available to customers.
184. An RRB must ensure that customers aren't compelled to drop the cheques in the drop-box.
Further, the RRB must invariably display on the cheque drop-box itself that "Customers can also tender the cheques at the counter and obtain acknowledgment on the pay-in slips".
The above message is required to be displayed in English, Hindi and the concerned regional language of the state.

188. An RRB must return/ despatch the dishonoured instruments to the customer promptly without delay, in any case within 24 hours.

An RRB must put in place an appropriate policy approved by its Board or Committee taking into consideration the need to prevent misuse of the cheque drawing facility and avoid penalising customers for unintended dishonour of cheques.
This policy must be transparent, made known to every customer upfront and implemented fairly.

The policy must also cover inherent preventive measures and checks to prevent any scope for collusion of the staff of the RRB or any other person, with the drawer of the cheque for causing delay in or withholding the communication of the fact of dishonour of the cheque to the payee / holder or the return of such dishonoured cheque to her / him.

The RRB must also lay down requisite internal guidelines for its staff and advise them to ensure strict compliance of it to achieve earlier object of effective communication and delivery of dishonoured cheque to the payee.

199. The lodger's bank must pay interest to the lodger for the delayed period in respect of collection of bills at the rate of 2 percent per annum above the rate of interest payable on balances of savings bank accounts.

The delayed period must be reckoned after making allowance for normal transit period based upon a time frame of two days each for (i) despatch of bills, (ii) presentation of bills of drawees, (iii) remittance of proceeds to the lodger's bank.

201. An RRB must be guided by Reserve Bank instructions on KYC / AML for opening and operation of accounts as prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025.

202. An RRB must be guided by Reserve Bank’s instructions on interest rates on deposit accounts and related matters as prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025.

203. An RRB must at the time of opening the accounts, inform its customers in a transparent manner, the requirement of maintaining minimum balance and details of charges, if any, due to non-maintenance of the same.
An RRB must inform, at least one month in advance, the existing account holders of any change in the prescribed minimum balance.

204. While levying charges for non-maintenance of minimum balance in savings bank account, an RRB must adhere to the instructions given below: (1) if a default in maintenance of minimum balance / average minimum balance as agreed to between the RRB and customer, the RRB must notify the customer clearly by SMS / email / letter etc. that if the minimum balance not being restored in the account within a month from the date of notice, penal charges will be applicable.

(2) In case the minimum balance isn't restored within a reasonable period, which must not be less than one month from the date of notice of shortfall, penal charges may be recovered under intimation to the account holder.
(4) The penal charges must be directly proportionate to the extent of shortfall observed.

In other words, the charges must be a fixed percentage levied on the amount of difference between the actual balance maintained and the minimum balance as agreed upon at the time of opening of account.
(6) It must be ensured that the balance in the savings account doesn't turn into negative balance solely on account of levy of charges for non-maintenance of minimum balance.

The cost of providing such passbook or statement of account must not be charged to the customers.

209. An RRB must avoid inscrutable entries in passbook / statement of account and ensure that brief, intelligible particulars are invariably entered in passbook / statement of account.

A printed slip requesting the depositor to tender their passbooks periodically must be given, especially in cases where a passbook is tendered for posting after a long interval of time or after very large number of transactions.

Further, the RRB must advise its branch inspecting officers to carry out sample check at the time of internal inspection of branches to verify whether the statements are being dispatched in time.

An RRB must adhere to the following instructions relating to operations in term deposit accounts: (1) An RRB must issue a term deposit receipt indicating in it full details, such as, date of issue, period of deposit, due date, applicable rate of interest, etc. (2) Term deposits must be freely transferable from one branch of the RRB to another.
(3) Change in interest rate on deposits must be made known to customers as well as bank branches expeditiously.
However, in no case must the amount or duration of the original term deposit undergo a change in any manner.

The policy must be non-discretionary and non-discriminatory.
The terms and conditions of renewal including interest rates must be notified to the customer at the time of acceptance of deposit.
However, the signatures of both the depositors may have to be obtained, in case the deposit is to be paid before maturity.
However, the signature of both the depositors may have to be obtained, in case the deposit is to be paid before maturity.
