231. On attaining the age of majority, fresh operating instructions and specimen signature of the account holder must be obtained and kept on record.
Moreover, if the account is operated by the guardian, the balance must be got confirmed.
An RRB must take advance action, including communicating these requirements to minor account holders attaining the age of majority, to ensure fulfilment of these requirements.
233. An RRB must ensure that accounts of minors, whether operated independently or through a guardian, aren't allowed to be overdrawn and that they always remain in credit balance.

234. An RRB must perform customer due diligence for opening of deposit accounts of minors and undertake ongoing due diligence, as per the rules in Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025.
235. An RRB must undertake at least an annual review in respect of accounts, where there is no customer-induced transaction for more than a year.

In cases where there is no explicit mandate to renew the term deposit, the RRB must review such accounts if the customers have not withdrawn the proceeds after maturity or transferred these to their savings / current account to prevent such deposits from becoming unclaimed.

The RRB must inform the account / deposit holders in writing through letters or email or SMS (if the email and mobile number are registered with the bank) that there has been no operation in their accounts / deposits in the last one year,.

The alert messages must invariably mention that the account would become ‘inoperative’ if no operations are carried out during the next one year and, the account holder would be required to submit KYC documents afresh for reactivating the account in such case.

236. If the letters are returned undelivered or no response is received through registered email, an RRB must immediately undertake an enquiry to find out the whereabouts of account holder or her / his nominee / legal heirs in case the account holder is deceased.
237. In case any response is received from the account holder giving the reasons for not operating the account, an RRB must continue to classify the account as operative for one more year.
In case the account holder still fails to operate the account within the extended period, an RRB must classify the said account as inoperative account after the expiry of the extended period.
238. For the purpose of classifying an account as ‘inoperative’, only customer induced transactions and not bank-induced transactions must be considered.
These transactions must also be treated as customer induced transactions.
239. The classification of an account as inoperative must be for a particular account of the customer and not with reference to the customer.

In case a customer is maintaining multiple accounts / deposits with a bank, all such accounts / deposits must be assessed individually for the purpose of classifying them as inoperative account / unclaimed deposit,.

An RRB must, based on the purpose of opening of the account, segregate the aforementioned accounts in its CBS, so that the stipulation of ‘inoperative’ account isn't applicable to these accounts due to their non-operation for a period of more than two years.
To avoid the risk of fraud, etc. in such accounts, while allowing operations in these accounts, an RRB must exercise due diligence as per the extant instructions.
242. The segregation of inoperative accounts is required to be done to reduce the risk of frauds.
The transactions in inoperative accounts, which have been reactivated, must be monitored regularly, for at least six months, at higher levels (i.e.
243. An RRB must ensure that amounts lying in inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits and reactivated inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits, are subjected to concurrent audit.
244. An RRB must contact the holder(s) of the inoperative account / unclaimed deposit through letters, email or SMS (if the email and mobile number are registered with the bank).
The email / SMS must be sent on a quarterly basis.

245. In case the whereabouts of the holder(s) of the inoperative account / unclaimed deposit aren't traceable, an RRB must contact the introducer, if any, who had introduced the account holder to the RRB at the time of opening of the account.
An RRB must also contact the nominee, if registered, for tracing the customer.
246. An RRB must undertake special drives periodically to find out the whereabouts of the customers, their nominees or legal heirs in respect of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits.
247. An RRB must make available the facility of updation of KYC for activation of inoperative accounts and unclaimed deposits at all branches (including non-home branches).
Further, the RRB must endeavour to provide the facility of updation of KYC in such accounts and deposits through Video-Customer Identification Process (V-CIP).
The V-CIP related instructions under Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 must be adhered to by the bank.

248. An RRB must activate the inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits, including those which are under freeze by orders of various agencies like courts, tribunals, law enforcement agencies, only after adhering to the KYC instructions provided in the Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 such as customer due diligence (CDD), customer identification, risk categorisation, etc. 249.
An RRB must ensure that activation of inoperative account / unclaimed deposits in CBS necessarily requires second level of authorisation by another officer at the same or higher level (i.e.
System logs must invariably be maintained in case of any activity in or activation of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits for concurrent audit purpose.
The preservation period of such system logs must be as per the internal guidelines of the bank.

250. An RRB must automatically intimate the inoperative account / unclaimed deposit holders through SMS and registered email stating that on the basis of the KYC documents submitted by them, the inoperative status of the account has been removed.
The intimation must also mention the remedial measures available to them to report unauthorised access, if any.
An RRB must have in place adequate operational safeguards to ensure that the claimants in case of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits are genuine.
An RRB must process requests for activation of inoperative account / unclaimed deposits within three working days from the receipt of the complete application.
251. Interest on savings accounts must be credited on a regular basis irrespective of the fact that the account is in operation or not.
252. An RRB must not levy penal charges for non-maintenance of minimum balances in any account that's classified as an inoperative account.
253. No charges must be levied for activation of inoperative accounts.

254. An RRB must host the details of unclaimed deposits {only name, address (without PIN code) and Unclaimed Deposit Reference Number (UDRN)}, which have been transferred to DEA Fund of Reserve Bank on its website, which must be updated regularly, at least on a monthly basis.
An RRB which doesn't have its own website must make available the above list of unclaimed deposits in its branches.
The database hosted on the website must provide a search option to enable the public to search for their unclaimed deposits using name in combination with the address of the account holder / entity.
Upon a successful search, details of unclaimed deposits must be displayed in a format comprising account holder’s name(s), her / his address (without PIN code) and UDRN only.
In case such accounts aren't in the name of individuals, the search input and result must include names of individuals authorised to operate the accounts.
However, the account number, its type, outstanding balance and the name of the branch must not be disclosed on the bank’s website.
255. An RRB must not allow any debit transaction in an inoperative account unless there is a customer-induced activation as per the procedure mentioned in paragraphs 247 to 250.
256. An RRB must ensure that there is no unauthorised access to customer data pertaining to the inoperative accounts.
An RRB must also ensure that adequate steps are taken to prevent data theft and related misuse for fraudulent purposes.
257. An RRB must provide on its website as well as at its branches, the information on the process for activation of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits and claiming the balances in it.

258. An RRB must conduct public awareness and financial literacy campaigns regularly to educate the members of public about the activation of inoperative accounts / unclaimed deposits and the prescribed procedure to claim amounts lying in it by a depositor or her / his nominee / legal heir in case of deceased depositor.

259. The instructions in this section must be applicable from January 1, 2022 (except where otherwise specified) to both new and existing safe deposit lockers and safe custody of articles facility provided by banks.
An RRB must put in place a comprehensive revised Board approved policy and SOPs on safe deposit locker facility / safe custody of articles as per the instructions mentioned here.
The due diligence must be carried out for all the customers in whatever rights and capacities they may be hiring the locker.
262. An RRB must incorporate a clause in the locker agreement that the locker-hirer/s must not keep anything illegal or any hazardous substance in the safe deposit locker.

If the RRB suspects the deposit of any illegal or hazardous substance by any customer in the safe deposit locker, the RRB must have the right to take appropriate action against such customer as it deems fit and proper in the circumstances.

263. An RRB must obtain recent passport size photographs of locker-hirer(s) and individual(s) authorised by locker hirer(s) to operate the locker and preserve them in the records pertaining to locker-hirer being maintained in the bank’s branch.

264. to facilitate customers making informed choices, an RRB must maintain a branch-wise list of vacant lockers as well as a waitlist in Core Banking System (CBS) or any other computerised system compliant with the cyber security framework issued by Reserve Bank, for the purpose of allotment of lockers and ensure transparency in allotment of lockers.
An RRB must acknowledge the receipt of all applications for allotment of locker and provide a waitlist number to the customers, if the lockers aren't available for allotment.
265. An RRB must have a Board approved agreement for safe deposit lockers.

The agreement must be in conformity with these instructions and the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the matter of ‘Amitabha Dasgupta vs United Bank of India’ (Judgment dated February 19, 2021 in CA No. 3966 of 2010).
An RRB must ensure that any unfair terms or conditions aren't incorporated in its locker agreements.
Further, the terms of the contract must not be more onerous than required in ordinary course of business to safeguard the interests of the RRB.
266. At the time of allotment of the locker to a customer, an RRB must enter into an agreement with the customer to whom the locker facility is provided, on a paper duly stamped.
A copy of the locker agreement in duplicate signed by both the parties must be furnished to the locker-hirer to know her / his rights and responsibilities.
Original agreement must be retained with the RRB’s branch where the locker is situated.

In such cases, all the provisions contained in this section, in particular paragraphs 297 to 299 on ‘Compensation Policy / Liability’, must continue to apply to them even if not explicitly stated in the agreements already executed.
Further, in such cases, the RRB must have the option to execute fresh agreements or revise them through supplementary agreements.
The cost of stamp paper in such cases must be borne by the RRB.
The RRB, however, must not insist on such term deposits from the existing locker holders or those who have satisfactory operative account.
The packaging of allotment of locker facility with placement of term deposits beyond what is specifically permitted above must be considered as a restrictive practice.
270. If locker rent is collected in advance, if surrender of a locker by a customer, the proportionate amount of advance rent collected must be refunded to the customer.

271. If there is any event such as merger / closure / shifting of branch warranting physical relocation of the lockers, an RRB must give public notice in two newspapers (including one local daily in vernacular language) in this regard.
In case of unplanned shifting due to natural calamities or any other such emergency situation, an RRB must make efforts to intimate its customers suitably at the earliest.
272. An RRB must take necessary steps to ensure that the area in which the locker facility is housed is properly secured to prevent criminal break-ins.
An RRB must have a single defined point of entry and exit to the locker room / vault.
The place where the lockers are housed must be secure enough to protect against hazard of rainwater / flood water entering and damaging the lockers in contingent situations.
The fire hazard risks of the area must also be assessed and minimised.
An RRB, as per its policy, must conduct necessary engineering / safety verification regularly to identify the risks and carry out necessary rectification.
273. The area housing the lockers must remain adequately guarded at all times.

An RRB must install an access control system, if required as per its risk assessment, which would restrict any unauthorised entry and create digital record of access to the locker room / vault with time log.

In case any customer has complained to the RRB that her / his locker is opened without her / his knowledge and authority, or any theft or security breach is noticed / observed, the RRB must preserve the CCTV recording till the police investigation is completed.
274. The security procedures must be well documented and the staff concerned must be properly trained in the procedure.
The internal auditors must verify and report the compliance to ensure that the procedures are strictly adhered to.

275. All new mechanical lockers to be installed by an RRB must conform to basic standards / benchmarks for safety and security as prescribed by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) or any other enhanced industry standards applicable in this regard.
In case the lockers are being operated through an electronic system, an RRB must take reasonable steps to ensure that the system is protected against hacking or any breach of security.
The customers’ personal data, including their biometric data, must not be shared with third parties without their consent.
Further, an RRB must ensure that the electronically operated lockers are compliant with the Cyber Security Framework prescribed by the Reserve Bank.
The system must be capable of maintaining unalterable log of locker activities.
An RRB must comply with the relevant statutory / regulatory instructions / requirements applicable for IT / data protection.

Further, an RRB must also devise a standard operating procedure for issue of new password in lieu of lost passwords to customers in a safe and secure manner in case of electronically operated lockers.

277. An RRB must ensure that identification Code of the RRB / branch is embossed on all the locker keys with a view to facilitating identification of lockers / locker ownership by law enforcement agencies in case of need.
Further, the custodian of the locker must, regularly / periodically, check the keys maintained in the branch to ensure that they are in proper condition.

An RRB must permit the locker-hirer to operate the locker only with the key provided by the RRB, although there is no restriction in allowing the customer to use an additional padlock of her / his own if there are such provisions in lockers.

278. The locker hirer and / or the persons duly authorised by him / her only must be permitted to operate the locker after proper verification of their identity and recording of the authorisation by the concerned bank officials.
The RRB must maintain a record of all individuals, including the locker-hirers, who have accessed the lockers.

The ingress and egress register for access to strong room / vault by locker-hirers or any other individual including the RRB’s staff must be maintained to record the movement of individuals in the strong room / vault area with their signatures at appropriate place in the records.
279. The RRB’s officer authorising the locker-hirer to access the locker, after unlocking the first key / password, must not remain present when the locker is opened by the locker-hirer.
The RRB must ensure that there is adequate privacy to the locker-hirers in the operations when customers access the lockers at the same time.

280. An RRB must send an email and SMS alert to the registered email address and mobile number of the customer before the end of the day as a positive confirmation intimating the date and time of the locker operation and the redressal mechanism available in case of unauthorised locker access.
281. There must be a system of inter-change of locks whenever the locker is surrendered by the hirer.
The keys of vacant lockers must be kept in sealed envelopes.
The duplicate master keys must be deposited with another branch of the RRB.
There must be proper record of joint custody of master keys.

An RRB must conduct surprise periodic verification of surrendered / vacant lockers and their keys by an officer of the RRB who isn't connected with their custody and proper record must be maintained as a proof of such verification.
282. An RRB must ensure that the Locker Register.
The Locker Register must be updated in case of any change in the allotment with complete audit trails.
283. The bank custodian must check whether the lockers are properly closed post locker operation.
If the same isn't done, the lockers must be immediately closed.
The bank custodian must record the fact of not closing the locker properly in the register and its closure by the RRB with the date and time.
Further, the custodian of the locker room must carry out a physical check of the locker room at the end of the day to ensure that lockers are properly closed.
285. An RRB must have a clear Board approved policy together with a SOP for breaking open the lockers for all possible situations keeping in view the relevant legal and contractual provisions.
286. If the key of the locker, supplied by the RRB is lost by the locker-hirer, the customer (locker-hirer) must notify the RRB immediately.
The charges applicable for replacement of lost keys / issue of new password must be communicated to the locker hirer.

287. The opening of the locker has to be carried out by the RRB or its authorised technician only after proper identification of the hirer, proper recording of the fact of loss and written authorisation by the customer for breaking open the locker.
288. The operation must be done in the presence of the customer(s) and an authorised official of the RRB.

It has to be ensured that the adjoining lockers aren't impacted by any such operations and the contents of the lockers aren't exposed to any individual other than the locker-hirer during the break open or restoration process.

289. In case of attachment and recovery of the contents in a locker of a customer or the articles left by a customer for safe custody of an RRB by any authority acting either under the orders of a court or any other competent authority vested with the power to pass such orders, the RRB must co-operate in execution and implementation of the orders.
290. The RRB must verify and satisfy itself about the orders and the connected documents received for attachment and recovery of the contents in a locker or articles in the safe custody of the RRB.

The customer (locker-hirer) must be informed by letter as well as by email / SMS to the registered email address / mobile phone number that the government authorities have approached for attachment and recovery or seizure of the locker or articles deposited for safe custody.
An inventory of the contents of locker and articles seized and recovered by the authority must be prepared in the presence of such government authorities, two independent witnesses.

291. An RRB must also record a video of the break-open process and the inventory assessment, wherever legally permissible, and preserve the video to produce as evidence in case of any dispute or court case or fraud case in future.
292. An RRB must have the discretion to break open any locker following due procedure if the rent has not been paid by the customer for three years in a row.
An RRB must ensure to notify the existing locker-hirer before any changes in the allotment and give her / him reasonable opportunity to withdraw the articles deposited by her / him.
293. Before breaking open the locker, an RRB must give due notice to the locker-hirer through a letter and through email and SMS alert to the registered email address and mobile phone number.
If the letter is returned undelivered or the locker-hirer isn't traceable, an RRB must issue public notice in two newspaper dailies (one in English.
The locker must be broken open in the presence of an officer of the RRB and two independent witnesses.

In case of electronically operated lockers (including smart vaults), the use of ‘Vault Administrator’ password for opening of locker must be assigned to a senior official and complete audit trail of access must be preserved.

Further, an RRB must also record a video of the break open process together with inventory assessment and its safe-keep and preserve the same so as to provide evidence in case of any dispute or court case in future.

The RRB must also ensure that the details of breaking open of locker is documented in CBS or any other computerised systems compliant with the cyber security framework issued by Reserve Bank, apart from locker register.
After breaking open of locker, the contents must be kept in sealed envelope with detailed inventory inside fireproof safe in a tamper-proof way until customer claims it.
A record of access to the fireproof safe must invariably be maintained.
While returning the contents of the locker, the RRB must obtain acknowledgement of the customer on the inventory list to avoid any dispute in future.
294. An RRB must ensure that the inventory prepared after breaking open of the locker is as per [***] 3 Annex X or as near to it as circumstances require.

Further, the RRB must not open sealed / closed packets left with them for safe custody or found in locker while releasing them to the nominee(s) and surviving locker hirers / depositor of safe custody article, unless required by law.

295. If the locker remains inoperative for a period of seven years and the locker-hirer can't be located, even if rent is being paid regularly, an RRB must be at liberty to transfer the contents of the locker to the nominee(s) / legal heir(s) of the locker-hirer or dispose of the articles in a transparent manner,.
Before breaking open the locker, an RRB must follow the procedure as prescribed in paragraphs 293 to 294 above.

An RRB must ensure that the procedure to be followed by them for disposal of the articles left unclaimed for a reasonably long period of time as mentioned above is incorporated in their locker agreement.
296. An RRB must ensure that appropriate terms are inserted in the locker agreement executed with the customer specifying the position in case the locker isn't in operation for long period.

297. An RRB must put in place a detailed Board approved policy outlining the responsibility owed by it for any loss or damage to the contents of the lockers due to its negligence as RRBs owe a separate duty of care to exercise due diligence in maintaining and operating its locker or safety deposit systems.

Further, the RRB must adhere to the Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Fraud Risk Management) Directions, 2026, as amended when needed, for reporting requirements about the instances of robberies, dacoities, thefts and burglaries.

298. An RRB must not be liable for any damage and / or loss of contents of locker arising from natural calamities or Acts of God like earthquake, floods, lightning and thunderstorm or any act that's attributable to the sole fault or negligence of the customer.
An RRB must, however, exercise appropriate care to its locker systems to protect its premises from such catastrophes.

As an RRB can't claim that it bears no liability towards its customers for loss of contents of the locker, in instances where loss of contents of locker is due to incidents mentioned above or attributable to fraud committed by its employee(s), the RRB’s liability must be for an amount equivalent to one hundred times the prevailing annual rent of the safe deposit locker.

300. An RRB, with the approval of its Board, must have a branch insurance policy to minimise the loss due to incidents like robbery, fire, natural calamities, loss during shifting / merger of branch, etc. affecting contents of lockers.

301. An RRB must clarify in its locker agreement that as it doesn't keep a record of the contents of the locker or of any articles removed therefrom or placed in it by the customer, they would not be under any liability to insure the contents of the locker against any risk whatsoever.
An RRB must under no circumstances offer, directly or indirectly, any insurance product to its locker hirers for insurance of locker contents.
302. An RRB must display the model locker agreement with all the terms & conditions.
An RRB must ensure that the customers are made aware of the bank’s terms and conditions to avail those facilities.
303. An RRB must display updated information on all kinds of charges for safe deposit lockers and safe custody articles on its website.

304. An RRB must place on its website, the instructions together with the policies / procedures put in place for giving access of the locker / safe custody article to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / legal heir(s) of the deceased locker hirer / safe custody article.
Further, a printed copy of the same must also be given to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / legal heir(s).

Accordingly, these directions are issued to banks to implement the nomination facility and must be read with sections 45ZA to 45ZG of The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and the Nomination Rules framed thereunder.
These Directions must be applicable from November 1, 2025.
306. An RRB must offer nomination facility in deposit accounts under sections 45ZA, 45ZB and 45ZG of the Act and the Rules.
307. An RRB must be guided by the rules in sections 45ZC to 45ZG of the Act and the Rules in the matter of nomination in safe deposit lockers and articles kept in safe custody.
Explanation: For the purpose of these Directions, it's clarified that if an individual is maintaining an account for her / his proprietorship business, it will be deemed as that individual’s account.

308. At the time of account opening, an RRB must explicitly inform the prospective customer of the availability and purpose of the nomination facility and offer her / him the option to avail the same.

The RRB must also clearly explain to the prospective customer the advantages of the nomination facility, including simplification of the claim process if the account holder’s demise and facilitation of smooth and prompt transfer of funds to the nominee without legal complications.

309. If the prospective customer chooses not to avail the nomination facility despite being fully informed, the RRB must proceed to open the deposit account without imposing any restrictions, if otherwise found eligible, after obtaining a written declaration from the individual confirming that she / he doesn't require the nomination facility at the time of account opening.
If she / he refuses to provide the written declaration, the RRB must record the fact of refusal to submit written confirmation in the account opening records.

310. Under no circumstances must a prospective customer be denied or delayed in opening an account solely on the ground of refusal to make a nomination, provided all other requirements for account opening are satisfactorily met.
311. In case of simultaneous nomination, if any nominee dies before receiving the deposit from an RRB, the nomination in respect of such nominee alone must become ineffective.

Accordingly, the RRB must settle the claims of the amount of deposit made in favour of such nominee as per provisions applicable for accounts without nominee clause as contained in paragraphs 328 to 335 of these Directions.
313. An RRB must have in place appropriate systems and procedures to register in its books the registration, cancellation and variation of the nomination, as per the request of the customers.
314. An RRB must devise proper systems for acknowledging the receipt of the duly completed forms of registration, cancellation and/ or variation of the nomination.
315. An RRB must verify and ensure that the nomination(s) made by its customers are as per relevant provisions of the Act and the Rules before providing acknowledgement to them.

316. Such acknowledgement must be given to the customers within three working days of receiving the forms of registration, cancellation and / or variation of nomination, irrespective of whether the same is asked for by the customers.

317. Where a nomination request is found not to be in conformity with the rules in the Act or the Rules and is consequently rejected, an RRB must inform the customer in writing, clearly indicating the reasons for such rejection, within three working days of the receipt of the request form.
318. An RRB must record the status regarding registration of nomination on the face of the passbook / statement of account and TDR, with the legend "Nomination Registered".
319. The RRB must also indicate the name of the nominee(s) in the passbook / statement of accounts and TDR in such cases.
320. An RRB must give wide publicity and provide guidance to deposit account holders, locker hirers and depositors of articles in safe custody on the benefits of the nomination facility.

321. An RRB must ensure that the form for opening deposit accounts, hiring safe deposit lockers and depositing articles in safe custody contains a space for getting the details of nomination, which also serves the purpose of educating the customers about availability of such facility.
323. The Directions in this section must be applicable from April 01, 2026.

These Directions must not be applicable in case of Government savings schemes administered by banks such as Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS), Public Provident Fund (PPF), etc. Settlement of claims in such cases must be as per the rules in the respective schemes.

324. For the limited purpose of Directions in this section, unless the context otherwise requires, the following definitions must apply: (1) ‘Customer’ refers to a person who may be a depositor or a locker hirer or has placed articles in safe custody with a bank.

325. A deposit account where a depositor had made nomination under the rules in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 or where the account was opened with survivorship clause, the payment of the outstanding balance upon the death of the depositor(s) to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) must be considered a valid discharge of an RRB’s liability, provided: (1) the RRB has exercised due care and caution in establishing the identity of the nominee(s) / survivor(s) and the deceased status of the account holder(s) by obtaining appropriate documentary evidence (physical or equivalent e-document).
Such payment to them must not affect the right or claim which any person may have against the nominee(s) / survivor(s) to the extent of the payment made to them.
327. Payment made to the nominee(s) / survivor(s), subject to the foregoing conditions, must constitute a full and valid discharge of a bank's liability.

Therefore, in such cases, while making payment to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) of the deceased depositor(s), an RRB must not insist on production of legal documents such as Succession Certificate, Letter of Administration, Probate of Will, etc. or seek any bond of indemnity / surety from the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / third-party, irrespective of the amount standing to the credit of the deceased account holder(s).
An RRB must require submission of the following documents in such cases: (1) Claim form, as given in Annex V, duly signed by the nominee(s) / survivor(s).

328. Keeping in view the imperative need to avoid inconvenience and undue hardship to the legal heir(s) / claimant(s), an RRB must follow a simplified procedure for settlement of claims in respect of deposit accounts where the aggregate amount payable, including accrued interest, as on the date of the application is less than the threshold limit, provided.

329. An RRB must settle the claim up to the threshold limit based on: (1) Claim form, as given in Annex VI, duly filled in and signed by the claimant(s) other than those who have signed the letter of disclaimer / no objection.
330. No bond of surety from a third-party must be obtained in case of claims up to the threshold limit.
331. In cases where claim amount is above the threshold limit, an RRB must settle the claim based on: (1) Succession Certificate and documents mentioned at paragraph 329(1) to 329(3) above; OR.
In such cases, the RRB must call for the documents at paragraph 329(1) to 329(5) above.

332. An RRB must settle claims involving ‘Will’ left behind by a deceased depositor on the basis of Probate of Will / Letter of Administration, in addition to documents mentioned at paragraph 329(1) to 329(3) above.
In cases where a person other than a legal heir is named as a beneficiary in the Will, applicable documents must also be obtained from her / him.
In such cases, an RRB must additionally call for the documents mentioned at paragraph 329(4) and 329(5) above.

334. In case of contesting claims or dispute amongst the legal heir(s) and / or the beneficiaries named in the Will of the deceased depositor, an RRB must settle claims on the basis of Probate of Will or Letter of Administration or Succession Certificate or Court order / decree, and the documents mentioned at paragraph 329(1) to 329(3) above.
Further, where there is an order from a Court restraining an RRB from making the payment, the claim must not be entertained during the period the order is in force.
The settlement of claim must be considered based on subsequent Court order to that effect.
335. No bond of surety must be insisted from a third party in cases falling under either E.1.2.2.1 or E.1.2.2.2 above.

336. Post settlement of the deposit account(s), in case any credit is received in the name of a deceased depositor, an RRB must return the same to the remitter with the remark 'Account holder deceased' and intimate the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / legal heir(s).

337. An RRB must incorporate a clause in the account opening form itself to the effect that if death of the depositor, premature termination of term deposits would be allowed without any penal charge, even if the deposit is within the lock-in-period.

338. Premature termination of term deposits opened jointly, with or without survivorship clause, must require the consent of the surviving depositor(s) and the legal heir(s) of the deceased joint holder, in case of death of one of the depositors.

However, in case of joint accounts with survivorship clause, if a specific mandate is furnished by all the depositors jointly to the RRB, either at the time of placing the term deposit or anytime subsequently during the tenure of the deposit, then premature withdrawal option must be allowed to the survivor(s) on the death of any of the depositors, without seeking the concurrence of the legal heir(s) of the deceased joint deposit holder.
339. The nominee(s) / legal heir(s) of a missing person must be required to get an order from the competent court under the rules in Sections 110 or 111 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
The claim in respect of such missing person must be settled as per the procedure applicable for settlement of claims in respect of a deceased customer.
In such cases, a copy of the court order declaring the civil death of the account holder must be obtained in lieu of the death certificate.

However, to avoid inconvenience and undue hardship to the common person where the aggregate amount payable, including accrued interest, as on the date of the application is less than ₹1 lakh or such higher amount as may be fixed by an RRB, a copy of the First Information Report (FIR) and non-traceable report issued by police authorities must be obtained in lieu of death certificate or an order from a competent court declaring the civil death of the account holder for settling the claim.

340. If a sole locker hirer nominates an individual(s) to receive the contents in the locker in case of her / his death, an RRB must give access to the locker to such nominee(s) with liberty to remove the contents of the locker.

341. In case the locker was hired jointly with the instructions to operate it under joint signatures, and the locker hirers nominate any other individual(s), if death of any of the locker hirers, an RRB must give access to the locker and the liberty to remove the contents jointly to the nominee(s) and the survivor(s).
342. In case the locker was hired jointly with survivorship clause.

343. In case of a minor nominee, an RRB must ensure that, the contents of locker, when sought to be removed on behalf of the minor nominee, are handed over to the guardian whose details have been provided in the nomination form.

If the details of the guardian have not been provided in the nomination form, an RRB must hand over the contents of the locker to a person who is, in law, competent to receive the contents of safe deposit locker on behalf of such minor.

344. The following documents must be obtained by an RRB for processing the claim in cases falling under paragraphs 340 and 341 above: (1) Claim form, as given in Annex V, duly signed by the nominee(s) / survivor(s).

345. An RRB must, however, ensure the following before giving access to the contents to the nominee(s) / survivor(s): (1) Exercise due care and caution in establishing the identity of the nominee(s)/ survivor(s) and deceased status of the locker hirer(s) by obtaining appropriate documentary evidence (physical or equivalent e-document).
Such access and liberty to remove the contents given to them must not affect the right or claim which any person may have against the nominee(s) / survivor(s) to whom the access is given.

346. After receipt of the documents mentioned at paragraph 344 above and being satisfied to the genuineness of the claim, the RRB must correspond with the nominee(s) / survivor(s) in writing and fix a date and time for making an inventory of the contents of the safe deposit locker.

The same must be undertaken in the presence of the nominee(s) and / or survivor(s) and / or their authorised representatives, two independent witnesses (should not be an employee or ex-employee of the RRB), the safe deposit vault custodian and another employee of the RRB not associated with locker operations, and recorded as per the inventory form given in Annex X.

The RRB must then hand over the possession of the contents of the locker to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / the person competent to receive the contents on behalf of the minor, and obtain an acknowledgment, as given in Annex X, that all the contents in the locker of the deceased hirer(s) have been removed.
Succession Certificate, Letter of Administration, Probate of Will, etc. or Bond of indemnity from the nominee(s) / survivor(s) must not be required unless there is any discrepancy in nomination.
348. Procedure, as prescribed in paragraphs 340 to 347 above, must be followed mutatis mutandis for return of articles kept by the deceased customer in the safe custody of the bank.
However, inventory form given in Annex XI must be used in such cases.

349. Keeping in view the imperative need to avoid inconvenience and undue hardship to the legal heir(s) / claimant(s), an RRB must adopt a simplified procedure for settlement of claims in safe deposit lockers provided there is no dispute amongst the legal heir(s) / claimant(s) and.

350. In cases falling under the simplified procedure, an RRB must obtain the following documents to settle the claim without obtaining any legal documents such as Succession Certificate, Letter of Administration, court order, etc. (1) Claim form, as given in Annex VI, duly filled and signed by the claimant legal heir(s).

351. An RRB must settle claims involving ‘Will’ left behind by a deceased safe deposit locker hirer on the basis of Probate of Will / Letter of Administration, in addition to documents mentioned at paragraphs 350(1) to 350(3) above.
In cases where a person other than a legal heir is named as a beneficiary in the Will, applicable documents must also be obtained from her / him.
In such cases, an RRB must additionally call for the documents mentioned at paragraphs 350(4) and 350(5) above.

353. Cases involving dispute amongst the legal heir(s) and / or beneficiaries named in the Will, must be settled based on Probate of Will or Succession Certificate or Letter of Administration or Court order / decree, and the documents mentioned at paragraphs 350(1) to 350(3) above.

354. After receipt of the required documents in claims falling under categories at E.2.2.1 and E.2.2.2 above and being satisfied as to the genuineness of the claim, the RRB must correspond with the claimant(s) in writing and fix a date and time for making an inventory of the contents of the safe deposit locker, as given in form prescribed in Annex X, in the presence of all claimant(s) or their duly authorised representatives, two independent witnesses (should not be an employee or ex-employee of the RRB), the safe deposit vault custodian and another employee of the RRB not associated with locker operations.
Valuation of the contents of the safe deposit locker must be carried out by an independent valuer and recorded in the Bond of Indemnity as given in Annex XII.

Bond of Indemnity must not be required to be given in cases of claims settled on the basis of legal documents such as Probate of Will or Succession Certificate or Letter of Administration or court order / decree, etc. 355.
Procedure, as prescribed in paragraphs 349 to 354 above, must be followed mutatis mutandis for return of articles kept by the deceased customer in the safe custody of the RRB.
However, inventory form given in Annex XI must be used in such cases.
356. An RRB must use the standardised forms for receiving the claims and other documents as per the formats provided in Annex V to Annex XII.

357. The standardised forms and other documents required for settlement of claims with respect to the deposit accounts / safe deposit locker / articles in safe custody kept by a deceased customer must be made available in all the branches as well as on the RRB’s website for the convenience of the claimant(s).
Further, the RRB must also display on its website, the list of documents to be submitted by a claimant and the procedure to be followed for settlement of claims in various scenarios.
358. A claimant must be allowed to lodge the claim at any of the branches against acknowledgment.
In case all required documents for processing of the claim have been submitted by the claimant, an RRB must also issue a confirmation in this regard.
However, in case of any pending or incomplete / incorrect documents, the RRB must intimate the claimant about the list of such documents while acknowledging the receipt of claim.
On subsequent submission of all the required documents, the RRB must issue a confirmation to the claimant that all required documents have been received for processing of the claim.

Upon a claimant uploading the claim form along with the required documents, the RRB must send acknowledgement / confirmation through appropriate channels and also make available the provision for online tracking of the status of the claim.
In such cases, if the RRB requires the claimant to produce original documents for submission / verification, the same must be allowed to be done at any of its branches.

360. An RRB must settle a claim in respect of deposit accounts of a deceased customer within a period not exceeding 15 calendar days from the date of receipt of all the required documents associated with the claim.

361. In case of safe deposit locker / articles in safe custody, an RRB must, within 15 calendar days of receipt of all the required documents, process the claim and communicate with the claimant(s) for fixing the date for making inventory of the locker / articles in safe custody.
362. If any deposit related claim isn't settled within the timeframe stipulated at paragraph 360 above, then an RRB must communicate the reasons for such delay to the claimant(s).

Further, in cases of delay attributable to the RRB, compensation must be paid by the RRB in the form of interest, at a rate not less than the prevailing Bank Rate + 4 per cent per annum, on the settlement amount due for the period of delay.
The reference date for reckoning the amount due and the prevailing Bank Rate must be the date of receipt of all required documents from the claimant.

363. For claims related to safe deposit locker / articles in safe custody, an RRB must be required to pay compensation to the claimant(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay, in cases where it doesn’t adhere to the timeline prescribed in paragraph 361 above.
Accordingly, an RRB must follow the procedure for settlement of claims in respect of such accounts as has been prescribed above for the accounts with / without nominee / survivorship clause,.

In such cases, an RRB must accept the original certified copy of the document issued for ‘proof of death’, certified in the country of its issuance in any one of the following modes: (1) Authorised officials of overseas branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India; or.

366. An RRB must continue to spread awareness among its customers about the benefits of the nomination facility / survivorship clause and give wide publicity to these facilities along with the procedure for settlement of claims.
367. An RRB must ensure that all information relating to charges / fees for processing are invariably disclosed in the loan application forms.
Further, an RRB must inform 'all-in-cost' to the customer to enable her / him to compare the rates and charges with other sources of finance.
368. The following instructions must be applicable in all new retail and MSME term loans sanctioned on or after October 1, 2024, including fresh loans to existing customers by an RRB.

Credit card receivables are exempted from the provisions given below: (1) The RRB must provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format given in the Annex XIII.
The KFS must be written in a language understood by such borrowers.
Contents of KFS must be explained to the borrower and an acknowledgement must be obtained that they have understood the same.

(2) The KFS must be provided with a unique proposal number and must have a validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than seven days.
The RRB must be bound by the terms of the loan indicated in the KFS, if agreed to by the borrower during the validity period.
(3) The KFS must also include a computation sheet of Annual Percentage Rate (APR), and the amortisation schedule of the loan over the loan tenor.

(4) Charges recovered from the borrowers by an RRB on behalf of third-party service providers on actual basis, such as insurance charges, legal charges etc. must also form part of the APR and must be disclosed separately.
In all cases wherever the RRB is involved in recovering such charges, the receipts and related documents must be provided to the borrower for each payment, within a reasonable time.
(6) The KFS must also be included as a summary box to be exhibited as part of the loan agreement.
369. An RRB must adhere to the following instructions for charging penal charges in respect of all the fresh loans availed from April 1, 2024 onwards.
In case of existing loans, the switchover to new penal charges regime must be applicable from June 30, 2024.

(1) Penalty, if charged, for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan contract by the borrower must be treated as ‘penal charges’ and must not be levied in the form of ‘penal interest’ that's added to the rate of interest charged on the advances.
There must be no capitalisation of penal charges, i.e.
Notes: (i) The material terms and conditions must be defined, if not already done, as per the credit policy of the RRB.

(ii) Default in repayment by the borrower is also a type of non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan repayment contract by the borrower and penalty, if charged, for such default must only be levied in the form of penal charges and not penal interest.
Such penal charges must be reasonable and levied by the RRB only on the amount under default in a non-discriminatory manner as per its Board approved policy.
Further, it must be ensured that there is no capitalization of the penal charges i.e.
(iii) Additional / Fresh penal charges must not be levied on the earlier outstanding amount of penal charges.
However, penalty, if any, on that funded facility on account of non-repayment by the borrower within the due date must only be levied in the form of penal charges and not penal interest.
(v) In respect of NPA accounts, penal charges must be reversed to the extent it remains uncollected for the specific purpose of non-recognition of income.
However, the same must be part of the total liability of the borrower to the RRB, unless it's waived as per the RRB's Board approved policy.
(vi) An RRB must disclose fees and charges, including penal charges, recovered from customers in 'Schedule 14: Other Income'.
(vii) An RRB must follow the instructions and clarifications, if any, issued by Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs (CBIC) with regard to applicability of GST on penal charges.
(2) An RRB must not introduce any additional component to the rate of interest and ensure compliance to these instructions in both letter and spirit.
(3) An RRB must formulate a Board approved policy on penal charges or similar charges on loans, by whatever name called.

(4) The quantum of penal charges must be reasonable and commensurate with the non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan contract without being discriminatory within a particular loan / product category.
The structure of penal charges within a particular loan / product category must have to be uniform irrespective of the constitution of the borrower.

(ii) Although no upper limit / cap for penal charges has been prescribed, the RRB, while formulating its Board approved policy on penal charges, must keep in mind that the intent of levying penal charges is essentially to inculcate a sense of credit discipline and such charges aren't meant to be used as a revenue enhancement tool.

(5) The penal charges in case of loans sanctioned to ‘individual borrowers, for purposes other than business’, must not be higher than the penal charges applicable to non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance of material terms and conditions.

(6) The quantum and reason for penal charges must be clearly disclosed by an RRB to the customers upfront in the loan agreement KFS, in addition to being displayed on the RRB’s website under 'Interest rates and Service Charges’.
Providing a reference to the schedule of penal charges displayed on the website of the RRB in the sanction letter and loan agreement must not suffice.
(7) Whenever reminders for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan are sent to borrowers, the applicable penal charges must be communicated.
Further, any instance of levy of penal charges and the reason therefor must also be communicated.

A bank must put in place an appropriate policy framework meeting the following requirements for implementation and compliance: (1) At the time of sanction, an RRB must clearly communicate to the borrowers about the possible impact of change in benchmark interest rate on the loan leading to changes in EMI and / or tenor or both.
Subsequently, any increase in the EMI/ tenor or both on account of the above must be communicated to the borrower immediately through appropriate channels.

(3) The borrowers must also be given the choice to opt for (i) enhancement in EMI or elongation of tenor or for a combination of both options; and, (ii) to prepay, either in part or in full, at any point during the tenor of the loan.
Levy of pre-payment charges must be subject to extant instructions.
Note: Whenever there is a reset of interest rates for an entire class of borrowers in a particular loan category, say home loan, due to increase in the reference benchmark.

(4) All applicable charges for switching of loans from floating to fixed rate and any other service charges / administrative costs incidental to the exercise of the above options must be transparently disclosed in the sanction letter and also at the time of revision of such charges / costs by the RRB when needed.
The applicable charges must be as approved by the Board and must be displayed on the RRB’s website.
(5) An RRB must ensure that the elongation of tenor in case of floating rate loan doesn't result in negative amortisation.

(6) An RRB must share / make accessible to the borrowers, through appropriate channels, a statement at the end of each quarter which must at the minimum, enumerate the principal and interest recovered till date, EMI amount, number of EMIs left and annualised rate of interest / APR for the entire tenor of the loan.
The RRB must ensure that the statements are simple and easily understood by the borrower.

In case of personal loans linked to an external benchmark under the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) regime, the RRB must follow extant instructions and also put in place adequate information systems to monitor transmission of changes in the benchmark rate to the lending rate.
372. In case of existing floating rate term loans sanctioned to individual borrowers on or before December 31, 2025, an RRB must not levy pre-payment charges.
373. An RRB must adhere to the following directions regarding levy of pre-payment charges on loans and advances (term loans as well as demand loans) sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
(1) For all floating rate loans granted for purposes other than business to individuals, with or without co-obligant(s), an RRB must not levy pre-payment charges.

(2) For all floating rate loans with sanctioned amount / limit up to ₹50 lakh granted for business purpose to individuals and Micro and Small Enterprises (as defined in Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006), with or without co-obligant(s), an RRB must not levy pre-payment charges.

(3) The Directions at paragraph 373(1) and 373(2) above must be applicable irrespective of the source of funds used for pre-payment of loans, either in part or in full, and without any minimum lock-in period.
(5) In cases other than those mentioned at paragraphs 373(1) and 373(2) above, pre-payment charges, if any, must be as per the approved policy of the RRB.
However, in case of term loans, pre-payment charges, if levied by the RRB, must be based on the amount being prepaid.
In case of cash credit / overdraft facilities, pre-payment charges on closure of the facility before the due date must be levied on an amount not exceeding the sanctioned limit.

(6) In case of cash credit / overdraft facilities, no pre-payment charges must be applicable if the borrower intimates the RRB of her / his / its intention not to renew the facility before the period as stipulated in the loan agreement, but the facility gets closed on the due date.
(7) An RRB must not levy any charges where pre-payment is effected at the instance of the RRB.
(8) The applicability or otherwise of pre-payment charges must be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement.
Further, in case of loans and advances where KFS is to be provided as specified in paragraph 368 above, the same must also be mentioned in the KFS.
No pre-payment charges which have not been disclosed as specified here must be charged by the RRB.
(9) An RRB must not levy any charges / fees retrospectively at the time of pre-payment of loans, which were waived off earlier by the RRB.

374. An RRB must release all the original movable / immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within a period of 30 days after full repayment / settlement of the loan account.

375. The borrower must be given the option of collecting the original movable / immovable property documents either from the banking outlet / branch where the loan account was serviced or any other office of the RRB where the documents are available, as per her / his preference.
376. The timeline and place of return of original movable / immovable property documents must be mentioned in the loan sanction letters issued on or after December 1, 2023.

377. to address the contingent event of demise of the sole borrower or joint borrowers, an RRB must have a well laid out procedure for return of original movable / immovable property documents to the legal heir(s).
Such procedure must be displayed on the website of the RRB along with other similar policies and procedures for customer information.

378. An RRB must communicate to the borrower reasons for delay in releasing of original movable / immovable property documents or failing to file charge satisfaction form with relevant registry beyond 30 days after full repayment / settlement of loan.
In case where the delay is attributable to the RRB, it must compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay.

379. In case of loss / damage to original movable / immovable property documents, either in part or in full, an RRB must assist the borrower in obtaining duplicate / certified copies of the movable / immovable property documents and must bear the associated costs, in addition to paying compensation as indicated at paragraph 378 above.
381. The Directions contained under this section must be applicable from April 1, 2026.

382. The policy on lending against gold and silver collateral, as required under Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 (here after referred to as ‘the policy’ in this section) / SOPs prepared under the policy must cover the conduct related aspects relating to: (1) assaying procedure of jewellery, ornaments, or coins made of gold and silver (“eligible collateral” for this section).

383. An RRB, which provides or intends to provide loans against eligible collateral, must ensure that a standardised procedure is put in place to assay the purity of gold and silver collateral, its weight (gross as well as net), etc. This procedure must be adopted uniformly across all its branches for all assaying procedures.

384. An RRB must display on its website the methodology adopted by it for determination of net weight of the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral and the price used to value the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral for determination of LTV ratio.
385. An RRB must ensure presence of the borrower(s) while assaying the collateral at the time of sanctioning the loan.

The deductions relating to stone weight, fastenings, etc. as part of the assaying procedure must be explained to the borrower(s) and details incorporated in the certificate to be issued as per paragraph 389 below.

386. Post pledging, cases involving loss of gold or silver collateral and any deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity observed during internal audit or otherwise including at the time of return or auction of collateral must be recorded and communicated promptly to the borrower(s)/ legal heir(s).
The process for making reimbursement or compensation as per the policy or SOP must also be communicated to the borrower(s)/ legal heir(s).
387. Documentation must be standardised across all branches of an RRB.

388. The loan agreement must cover the description of the eligible collateral taken as security, value of such collateral, details of auction procedure and the circumstances leading to the auction of the eligible collateral, the notice period which must be allowed to the borrower for repayment or settlement of loan before the auction is conducted, timelines for release of pledged eligible collateral upon full repayment or settlement of loan, refund of surplus, if any, from the auction of the pledged eligible collateral and other necessary details.
All applicable charges payable by the borrower, including those related to assaying, auction, etc. must be clearly included in the loan agreement and KFS.

389. An RRB, while accepting the eligible collateral, must prepare a certificate or e-certificate in duplicate on its letterhead regarding the assay of the collateral and state in it the purity (under carats); gross weight of the eligible collateral pledged; net weight of gold or silver content in it and deductions, if any, relating to weight of stones, lac, alloy, strings, fastenings, etc. damage, breakage or defects, if any, noticed in the collateral; image of the collateral; and the value of collateral arrived at the time of sanction (as per the instructions on valuation and assaying of Gold and Silver collateral specified in the Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025).
One copy of the certificate or e-certificate must be kept as part of the loan documents.

390. All communication with the borrower, especially, the terms and conditions of the loan, or other important communication which affects the interest of the borrower or the RRB, must be in the language of the region or in a language as chosen by the borrower.
For an illiterate borrower, important terms and conditions must be explained in the presence of a witness, who must not be an employee of the RRB.

391. An RRB must ensure that necessary infrastructure and facilities are put in place and appropriate security measures taken in each of its branches where loans are sanctioned against gold and / or silver collateral.
392. An RRB must ensure that the gold and / or silver collateral is handled only in its branches and only by its employees.
393. An RRB must store the collateral only in its branches which are manned by its employees and having safe deposit vaults fit for storing gold and silver.
Normally, such loans must not be extended by branches that don't have appropriate secured facility for storage of the pledged eligible collateral.

395. An RRB must periodically review the adequacy of systems for storage of the eligible collateral, conduct training of the concerned staff and carry out internal audit of all procedures to ensure that these are strictly adhered to.
396. As part of internal audit, an RRB must carry out periodic surprise verification of the gold and silver collateral pledged with it and must maintain a record of it.

A clause in the loan agreement must be included for obtaining consent of the borrower(s) to carry out surprise verification including assay of the pledged eligible collateral even in their absence during the tenor of the loan.
This aspect must be specifically communicated to the borrower at the time of sanctioning the loan.

397. An RRB must release or return the pledged eligible collateral held as security to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) on the same day but in any case, not exceeding a maximum period of seven working days upon full repayment or settlement of the loan.

398. At the time of release of pledged eligible collateral to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s), the collateral must be verified for correctness as per details in the certificate (as per paragraph 390) to the borrowers’ satisfaction.
399. An RRB must give adequate notice to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s), through available means of communication to repay or settle the loan dues before initiating the auction procedure.
A copy of the notice and acknowledgement of it must be kept on record in both scenarios.

400. An RRB must implement a transparent auction procedure, which must include, among other things, announcement of the auction to the public by issue of advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.
401. The pledged eligible collateral must be auctioned by an RRB only through its employee having necessary experience and / or training or an auctioneer empanelled by an RRB as per its policy.

In cases where auctions are conducted by the RRB through its employees, necessary safeguards such as surprise visits by regional / controlling officials on periodic basis, coverage under internal audit, etc. must be put in place.
402. An RRB must declare a reserve price for the gold and silver collateral at the time of auction, which must not be less than 90 per cent of its current value.
But in case auctions fail twice, a reserve price not less than 85 per cent of its current value must be adopted.
403. The first auction must be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located.
404. As a matter of policy, the RRB or its related parties must not participate in the auctions to ensure that there is no potential conflict of interest.
405. After the auction, the RRB must mandatorily provide full details of the value fetched at the auction and the dues adjusted to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

The surplus, if any, from the auction of the gold or silver collateral, must be refunded to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) within a maximum period of seven working days from the date of receipt of the full auction proceeds.
406. In case of any damage to the pledged eligible collateral by an RRB during the tenor of loan, the cost of repair must be borne by the RRB.

407. In case of loss of the pledged eligible collateral and / or any loss emanating from deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity observed during internal audit or otherwise including at the time of return or auction of collateral, an RRB must suitably compensate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

408. In case of delay in release of the pledged collateral after full repayment or settlement of loan by the borrower, where reasons for delay are attributable to an RRB, the RRB must compensate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay beyond the timeline prescribed at paragraph 397 above.
If the delay isn't attributable to an RRB, it must communicate reasons for such delay to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

Further, where the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) has not approached an RRB for release of pledged eligible collateral after full repayment or settlement of loan, the RRB must issue periodic reminders to borrower(s) / legal heir(s) through letters, email or SMS if the email and mobile number are registered with the bank.
409. The compensation provided under paragraphs 406 to 408 above must be without limiting the rights of a borrower / legal heir to get any other compensation as per any applicable law.
410. The pledged gold or silver collateral lying with an RRB beyond two years from the date of full repayment or settlement of loan must be treated as unclaimed.
An RRB must periodically undertake special drives to ascertain the whereabouts of the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) in respect of such unclaimed gold and / or silver collateral.
411. A report on unclaimed gold and silver collateral must be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board, at half-yearly intervals for a review.
412. An RRB must refrain from issuance of misleading advertisements containing unrealistic claims to promote loans against gold or silver collateral.

413. An RRB must ensure that all arrangements for sourcing and / or recovery of loans against eligible collateral, are in compliance with applicable directions on outsourcing and recovery practices issued by the Reserve Bank.

414. For prudential related aspects, the RRB must be guided by the instructions contained in the Chapter on ‘Lending against Gold and Silver Collateral’ in Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
415. A Fair Practices Code (FPC) for microfinance loans based on these directions must be put in place by an RRB with the approval of its Board.
The FPC must be displayed by the RRB in all its branches and on its website.
The FPC must be issued in a language understood by the borrower.
416. There must be a standard form of loan agreement for microfinance loans in a language understood by the borrower.
417. An RRB must provide a loan card to the borrower which must incorporate the following: (1) Information which adequately identifies the borrower.
418. All entries in the loan card must be in a language understood by the borrower.
419. Issuance of non-credit products must be with full consent of the borrowers and fee structure for such products must be explicitly communicated to the borrower in the loan card itself.
420. There must be no pre-payment charge on microfinance loans.
Charges, if any, for delayed payment must be applied on the overdue amount and not on the entire loan amount.

421. An RRB must prominently display the minimum, maximum and average interest rates charged on microfinance loans in all its offices, in the literature (information booklets / pamphlets) issued by it and details on its website.
This information must also be included in the supervisory returns and subjected to supervisory scrutiny.
422. Any change in interest rate or any other charge must be informed to the borrower well in advance.
424. Reserve Bank must also make available information regarding interest charged by RRBs on microfinance loans.
425. An RRB must have a Board-approved policy regarding the conduct of employees and system for their recruitment, training and monitoring.
This policy must, among other things, lay down minimum qualifications for the staff and must provide necessary training tools to deal with the customers.
Training to employees must include programs to inculcate appropriate behaviour towards customers.
Conduct of employees towards customers must also be incorporated appropriately in their compensation matrix.
426. Field staff must be trained to make necessary enquiries regarding the income and existing debt of the household.
427. Training, if any, offered to the borrowers must be free of cost.

428. An RRB must put in place a mechanism for identification of the borrowers facing repayment related difficulties, engagement with such borrowers and providing them necessary guidance about the recourse available.
429. Recovery must be made at a designated / central designated place decided mutually by the borrower and the RRB.

However, field staff must be allowed to make recovery at the place of residence or work of the borrower if the borrower fails to appear at the designated / central designated place on two or more successive occasions.
430. An RRB or its agent must not engage in any harsh methods towards recovery.
Without limiting the general application of the foregoing, following practices must be deemed as harsh: (1) Use of threatening or abusive language.
431. An RRB must have a dedicated mechanism for redressal of recovery related grievances.
The details of this mechanism must be provided to the borrower at the time of loan disbursal.
433. An RRB must have a due diligence process in place for engagement of recovery agents, which must, among other things, cover individuals involved in the recovery process.
An RRB must ensure that the recovery agents engaged by it carry out verification of the antecedents of its employees, which must include police verification.
An RRB must also decide the periodicity at which re-verification of antecedents must be resorted to.
434. To ensure due notice and appropriate authorisation, an RRB must provide the details of recovery agents to the borrower while initiating the process of recovery.
The agent must also carry a copy of the notice and the authorisation letter from the RRB along with the identity card issued to her / him by the RRB or the agency.

Further, where the recovery agency is changed by an RRB during the recovery process, in addition to the RRB notifying the borrower of the change, the new agent must carry the notice and the authorisation letter along with her / his identity card.
435. The notice and the authorisation letter must, among other details, also include the contact details of the recovery agency and the RRB.
436. The up-to-date details of the recovery agencies engaged by an RRB must also be hosted on its website.

437. An RRB must strictly ensure that it or its agents don't resort to intimidation or harassment of any kind, either verbal or physical, against any person in their debt collection efforts, including acts intended to humiliate publicly or intrude upon the privacy of the debtors' family members, referees and friends, sending inappropriate messages either on mobile or through social media, making threatening and / or anonymous calls, persistently calling the borrower and / or calling the borrower before 8:00 a.m.
438. Standing instructions must be freely accepted on all current and savings bank accounts.
440. All transactions, including payment of interest on deposits / charging of interest on advances, must be rounded off to the nearest rupee i.e.
Fractions of 50 paise and above must be rounded off to the next higher rupee and fraction of less than 50 paise must be ignored.
441. Issue prices of cash certificates must also be rounded off in the same manner.
The RRB must ensure that appropriate action is taken against members of its staff who are found to have refused to accept cheques / drafts containing fractions of a rupee.
443. An RRB must extend necessary help / co-ordination to tax officials whenever required.
Further, the RRB must view with serious concern cases where its staff connives / assists in any manner with offences punishable under the Income Tax Act.
In such cases, in addition to the normal criminal action, such staff member must also be proceeded against departmentally.
All approvals or acknowledgments granted under these repealed lists must be deemed as governed by these Directions.
